text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended mixed in quiet trading. August was the most active month, with 755 of a total of 1,746 lots done. The contract lost 30 cents to close at $321.0 per tonne, while October added 60 cents to close at $316.20 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended higher across the board. October and March added 5 points to close at 11.19 and 11.23 cents/lb respectively. The spot month went out 8 cents/lb firmer at 11.00 cents/lb, having ranged from 11.14 to 10.88 cents/lb. The bulk of the day's volume estimated at only 15,718 lots, centered on the July contract.

Traders said activity should remain quiet for the rest of the week due to Friday's 4th of July holiday. In Asia Thai premiums rose on lingering concerns over possible tighter supplies caused by insufficient rain. Even though the amount of rain has increased recently, industry sources said concerns remained over supplies as many believed that the lack of rain during May and June would damage the quality of sugar cane in many areas.

BRAZIL - Sugar cane production in the Center South up to June 1 reached 32.90 million tonnes, 19.12 percent more than was produced the same period in 1996/97. Sugar production reached 1.23 million tonnes, tel quel, up 32.26 percent. In spite of the sharp rise in the first weeks of 1997/98 sugar production in the Center South of Brazil is still forecast to rise by not more than between 4 and 6 percent.

BRAZIL - Sugar exports in May 1997, the first month of the 1997/98 campaign (May/April), amounted to 246,253 tonnes, raw value, up from 182,499 tonnes in May 1996. Total exports in 1996/97 reached 5.368 million tonnes compared to 5.922 million tonnes in 1995/96. Major countries of destination in May 1997 were Russia with 31,235 tonnes whites against 14,000 tonnes and 46,847 tonnes raws compared to nil, the USA with 48,596 tonnes raws against 45,322, the United Arab Emirates with 21,000 tonnes raws against nil and Nigeria with 20,142 tonnes whites against 21,127.

SOUTH AFRICA - Sugar production is forecast to reach 2.540 million tonnes in 1997/98 (May/April), up from 2.269 million tonnes produced the previous year. Sugar consumption in 1997/98 is forecast to rise slightly to 1.363 million tonnes, up from 1.344 million tonnes in 1996/97 and 1.278 million tonnes in 1995/96.

GERMANY - Sugar production in May 1997 amounted to 2,312 tonnes, raw value, up from 1,850 tonnes in May 1996. This brought cumulative production in the first eight months of 1996/97 (October/May) up to 4.550 million tonnes against 4.144 million in 1995/96. Total production in 1995/96 reached 4.158 million tonnes compared to 3.991 million tonnes in 1994/95. Sugar consumption in May 1997 amounted to 245,136 tonnes, down from 261,984 tonnes in May 1996.

This brought cumulative consumption in the first eight months of 1996/97 (October/May) up to 1.960 million tonnes compared to 1.971 million tonnes in 1995/96. Total consumption in 1995/96 reached 3.076 million tonnes, up from 2.995 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 2.940 million tonnes in 1993/94.

CZECH REPUBLIC - Sugar exports in May 1997 amounted to 6,545 tonnes, raw value, up from 1,585 tonnes in May 1996. This brought cumulative exports in September/May 1996/97 up to 60,567 tonnes, up from 18,787 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 27,684 tonnes compared to 35,029 tonnes in 1994/95.
